title: Our New T and L Framework
author: Pedagogy Geek
summary: This short post from the Pedagogy Geek Substack describes how a school introduced a new Teaching and Learning framework to staff during its start-of-year inset day. The framework is built on the principles of the book Making Every Lesson Count, lightly adapted after feedback gathered on LinkedIn, with the author deliberately choosing to keep most of the original intact because the principles are research informed and already proven in many schools. The piece explains the rationale given to staff: the framework is meant to act as a backbone behind CPD, lesson visits and coaching conversations, and to create a shared language among teachers and with students. Two local additions stand out: digital literacy and multilingualism are threaded across the whole framework rather than treated as standalone initiatives, reflecting the school's development priorities. Because staff teach across primary and secondary, a single cross-phase framework is presented as a unifying tool. The post ends by inviting other leaders to share how they use such frameworks to drive and assess improvement.
points: The school adopted the Making Every Lesson Count principles almost unchanged, reasoning that research-informed principles already working in many schools did not need reinvention.
The framework is positioned as the connective tissue for CPD, lesson visits and coaching, giving staff and students a consistent instructional vocabulary.
A spot-the-difference activity was used at inset to surface the few local adaptations and emphasise how little was changed.
Digital literacy and multilingualism were woven across every element rather than bolted on, signalling they are whole-school responsibilities.
A single framework spanning primary and secondary was chosen to support staff who teach across both phases.
quotes: During our inset at the start of this year, we introduced our new Teaching and Learning framework to staff. We started with the principles from the excellent book, Making every lesson count.
In the end, we made a couple of changes to fit our context, but decided to keep majority of it the same.

When we introduced it to staff, we began by explaining why we are introducing this framework which includes creating a backbone lying behind our CPD, lesson visits and coaching conversations, ensuring consistency in the language we use between us as teachers and with students. This framework will enable us to identify clear areas of focus by constantly referring to these key elements.

We used a spot the difference as an introduction to highlight our changes but also the fact that there aren’t many! These principles are brilliant and already used by many schools because they are research informed and they work!

Adding digital literacy and multilingualism running across the framework, areas we are focusing on developing across the school, highlights that these are not stand alone. We will be embedding these into all areas of the framework continuing to develop our approach to digital literacy while supporting multilingual learners.
We have staff who teach across primary and secondary, so a framework across both supports all staff and I am excited to see how it develops!
